conviction_note: The evidence is balanced, so p_up is 50 and the scaled move is 0. On the positive side: third-party DAU tracking runs at or slightly above a consensus that already assumes about 26% DAU growth, and short interest is crowded at 15% of shares and 8.5 days to cover. On the negative side: five straight negative print reactions in which DAU beats were sold on monetization and guidance; a likely bonus accrual if Q4 DAU growth reaches 25%, which would cut the EBITDA guide; and Super Lite / Max tier changes that are an ARPU risk to the bookings guide. The findings sum to +0.2, consistent with the zero.

EBITDA $76M (25.2%); FY26 bookings $1,285M, revenue $1,207M, adj. EBITDA margin 26.5%. MarketBeat consensus EPS $0.569 / revenue $303.22M (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-11-3-duolingo-inc-stock/); Earnings Whispers EPS $0.55, whisper $0.52 (finviz preview 2026-10-26). The bar is sourced to the company guide plus agreeing estimate sources. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against about $304M consensus revenue / $309M bookings.
positioning_check: Short interest 7,103,345 shares at the 2026-10-15 FINRA settlement (prior 7,152,857), 8.47 days to cover on 839k ADV, about 15.2% of the 46.79M Class A shares outstanding (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/duol/shortinterest). A separate aggregator showed 7.15M shares / 6.7 days at the 2026-09-30 settlement. This is a crowded short, so negatives were shrunk. The 25-delta skew was rejected by the baseline (46.5 vol points flagged implausible), so there is no usable directional skew. Put/call OI is 0.75 (call-heavy). ATM IV is 167.6%; event-implied move 13.54%. The stock is down 8.6% over 20 days, 4.2% over 5 days, about 15% from about $159 on 2026-09-01, and 49% below its 52-week high.

findings.finding: Third-party DAU tracking points to Q3 DAU growth at or slightly above the 63.49M (+25.7%) consensus. D.A. Davidson's panel of over 170k users implied Q3 DAU growth of 25.6-27.6% y/y (August DAUs +1.3% m/m), against 23% in Q2 and a company FY assumption of about 20%. A 2026-11-03 Investing.com preview says unnamed analysts' proprietary data show October trends pointing to further DAU acceleration, which could prompt a DAU guide raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-05): DAUs accelerated to +23% and beat the company's expectations; the stock fell 9.41% on a moderate revenue guide. Q3 2025 (2025-11-05): DAUs +36%; the stock fell 25.49% when management prioritised users over monetization. This name has sold DAU beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The 63.49M DAU consensus (+25.7%) already sits inside the panel range, so only the top half of that range (above about 26%) and any October acceleration feeding a raised DAU guide would be news. If the market were paying for the DAU tracking, the stock would not be down about 15% since the Sep 1-2 upgrades.
findings.independence: Investing.com preview 2026-11-03 (https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/duolingo-earnings-on-deck-can-user-growth-justify-margin-tradeoff-93CH-4926363) cites October proprietary data pointing to acceleration. The 2026-08-18 D.A. Davidson upgrade (https://pro.edgex.exchange/en-US/news/article/duolingo-stock-jumps-after-da-davidson-upgrade) said +24% from data through mid-August. Both rest on broker panels, not on company data.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-08-05) management disclosed a bonus plan that pays about $10M in cash, more if growth is higher, if Q4 2026 DAU growth reaches 25%; it is excluded from FY guidance. With tracking at 25.6-27.6% for Q3 and October reportedly accelerating, an accrual in Q3/Q4 is likely. That would push Q3 adj. EBITDA below the $76M guide and/or trim the FY 26.5% margin guide by about 0.8 points.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin guides were punished: the FY26 guide with a margin squeeze (2026-02-26) fell 14.01%, and the January 2026 preliminary print plus CFO exit fell 8.45%. The Q2 raise of the EBITDA margin outlook by nearly a point did not stop a 9.41% fall.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The plan is public but excluded from guidance, and the EBITDA consensus has not been visibly cut (EPS consensus was revised down only 0.4% in 30 days per Zacks). If it were priced, Q3 EBITDA and EPS consensus would sit about $5M under the company's $76M guide.
findings.independence: Investing.com preview 2026-11-03 (https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/duolingo-earnings-on-deck-can-user-growth-justify-margin-tradeoff-93CH-4926363) independently says the bonus would be recognised in Q3 and Q4 and temporarily depress EBITDA margins. That preview shares the DAU-tracking premise with finding 1, so this finding is the same DAU strength read through its cost. The two are sized for opposite effects and do not double-count.

findings.finding: Monetization lags users, which is a risk to the Q4 bookings guide. Q3 bookings were guided to only +8.9% ($307M, consensus $309.05M) and FY bookings were not raised despite DAU acceleration. In August the CEO said Max might be sunset, and a 'Super Lite' tier at about half Super's price (ads, limited Energy; $35.99/yr seen on iPhone 2026-09-06) was in test. Both are ARPU / mix headwinds to bookings per DAU going into the Q4 and 2027 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Every one of the last five reactions (-9.41, -5.62, -14.01, -8.45, -25.49) followed a release where bookings or revenue guidance, or a monetization trade-off, disappointed while users were fine.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The guide is public and the stock is 49% off its high, so this finding rests on the tier test and the Max decision not being reflected in the Q4 bookings consensus. If the market expected an ARPU hit, bookings consensus would be at or below guide rather than $2M above it.
findings.independence: The Max-sunset / Super Lite reporting is from a review site summary of the CEO's Q2 call comments (search result 'Language App Guide', checked 2026-09-06) and was not verified against the transcript. The finviz/Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-10-26 (https://finviz.com/news/408330/duolingos-user-rebound-faces-a-test-can-q3-show-bookings-catching-up-to-daus) frames the same bookings-vs-DAU gap.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-03/04 Duolingo and Bharti Airtel announced 12 months of Super Duolingo free for Airtel's roughly 376M Indian subscribers, activated in the Airtel Thanks app with no card. This is likely a September-onward DAU and possibly paid-subscriber lift in India at low or unknown ARPU.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior telco bundle; India is a low-ARPU market. DAU lines have not been rewarded (see finding 1).
findings.why_not_priced: The deal's economics (wholesale fee or not, whether bundle users count as paid subscribers) are undisclosed, so neither consensus subs (13.12M) nor bookings can reflect it. If priced, the paid-sub consensus would show a step-up beyond trend.
findings.independence: indiantelevision.com (https://indiantelevision.com/iworld/duolingo-partners-with-airtel-to-give-subscribers-a-free-12-month-super-duolingo-subscription/) reports the same deal. This is a proxy: the company has not quantified any impact.

findings.finding: FX: Q3 guidance was set at July 31 rates, and the company says each 1% move in the dollar is worth about $4M of H2 bookings. The DXY fell from about 100.35 (end July) to 99.55 (end August) and was roughly flat over the quarter; USD/JPY fell 3.2% in Q3, and Japan is a large market. That gives a small Q3 bookings tailwind of about $1-2M. A reported October dollar rebound would be a small headwind to the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of FX driving a reaction on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Too small to matter. It would show up as a $1-2M bookings beat inside normal guide conservatism.
findings.independence: NAGA Q3 review (https://naga.com/za/news-and-analysis/articles/forex-market-outlook): DXY +0.2% over Q3, USD/JPY -3.2%. FX sensitivity is from the Q2 letter. Macro-to-company proxy.

findings.finding: Crowded short into the print: 7.10M shares short (about 15.2% of Class A shares outstanding) and 8.47 days to cover at the 2026-10-15 settlement. With the stock about 15% below its early-September level and 49% off its high, a print without a guide cut has squeeze fuel.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest peaked at 8.73M at the 2026-02-27 settlement, right after a -14.01% print, so shorts were paid on the last cycle. The only up reactions in eight prints (+21.61 May 2025, +13.75 Aug 2025) came when guidance surprised up.
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning itself, a mechanism rather than a fact. It is priced only to the extent the call-heavy OI (put/call 0.75) and 167% ATM IV already embed squeeze risk.
findings.independence: Massive.com reported 7.15M short / 6.7 days at the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/duol).

findings.finding: CEO Luis von Ahn sold about 226,000 shares (about $34M) at $150-152 between 2026-09-16 and 2026-10-07 under a 10b5-1 plan, cutting direct holdings to about 5k shares (trust holdings not shown). The General Counsel and a director also sold in September. There were no open-market buys in Aug-Nov.
findings.why_not_priced: Public Form 4s on pre-arranged plans carry little information, so this is near zero by construction.
findings.independence: capital.com Form 4 summaries (https://capital.com/en-gb/news/duolingo-ceo-luis-von-ahn-disposes-of-usd-6-95-million) report the same filings.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew (rejected as implausible). The negative run-up (-8.6% over 20 days, about -15% since Sep 1) and the crowded short lean toward a rebound, while the name's five straight negative reactions lean the other way. The findings offset, so nothing cuts strongly against the baseline.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): DAU-tracking finding cut from +0.8 to +0.5 because this name sold DAU beats in Q2 2026 (-9.4%) and Q3 2025 (-25.5%).
Lesson 7 (crowded short, 15% of shares, 8.5 days to cover): negatives shrunk once each, bonus/EBITDA -0.8 to -0.6, monetization/guide -0.7 to -0.5, insider sales -0.2 to -0.1.
Lesson 5 (proxies filed small): Airtel and FX already small and labelled as proxies; unchanged.
Lesson 6 (bar sourced to the company guide plus agreeing estimates; class-action deadline moved to outside_window): no size change.
